summary: Senica District (okres Senica) is a district in the Trnava Region of western Slovakia. The note describes it as relatively rich in natural resources such as oil, gas and lignite, and as an industrial district where new industrial facilities were established in the later period. The district took its present borders in 1996, with the town of Senica serving as its seat, largest town, and administrative, cultural and economic center. Notable sites include the Smrdáky spa and the basilica in Šaštín.
one_line: Senica District is an industrial district in western Slovakia's Trnava Region, rich in oil, gas and lignite, with its present borders dating from 1996.
key_facts: Senica District (okres Senica) is a district in the Trnava Region of western Slovakia.
The district is relatively rich in natural resources: oil, gas and lignite.
Senica District is an industrial district, and in the late period new industrial facilities were established there.
Senica District in its present borders was established in 1996.
The town of Senica is the seat of Senica District.
Senica is the largest town in Senica District.
Senica is the administrative, cultural and economic center of Senica District.
The spa Smrdáky is located in Senica District.
The basilica in Šaštín is of cultural importance and is located in Senica District.
